title: Anthropic's automated researchers close a model's alignment gaps on their own - TCR 08/29/26
description:
Anthropic's automated researchers improved a model on all 10 alignment benchmarks while its best method scored about 20% higher than proposals from 28 human safety experts on the study's deception-mitigation score, Z.ai released GLM-5.3's full 756GB open weights alongside Tencent's 770B-parameter Hy4 and Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, and a CD19 CAR-T therapy put 3 of 6 treatment-refractory rheumatoid arthritis patients into medication-free remission.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-august-29-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:42 Anthropic's automated researchers fix a model's alignment gaps
3:43 Meta's robots reach the data-center floor
6:43 California opens the grid to household power
9:38 Parts of Gary go dark while some data centers stay lit
12:26 A cancer cell therapy crosses into autoimmune disease
15:09 Close

This episode covers Anthropic's self-improving alignment loop and its comparison of estimated specialist labor near $150 an hour with about $4 an hour in model-compute costs, Meta testing Watney and Kinova robots inside its data centers as one tracker found that automation was named as a driver in over half of documented 2026 layoff events, California's SB 913 and balcony solar bills opening the grid to household power, the Gary Indiana blackout during which some data centers reportedly stayed online while 63,000 customer accounts lost power, and a first-in-kind CAR-T trial crossing from cancer into autoimmune disease.

Anthropic's fellows program published a paper showing an automated loop that reads the alignment literature, proposes fixes, trains a model, tests it, and keeps what works - improving performance in all ten tested alignment-failure settings without measurable losses on the study's capability evaluations and generalizing to models up to 4.7 times larger. The comparison that carries it: on the study's deception-mitigation score, the best automated method outscored proposals from 28 experienced human safety researchers, at roughly $4 an hour in model-compute costs, compared with estimated specialist labor near $150 an hour. The same day, three frontier-adjacent open models landed in a single week, a cancer cell therapy improved every patient in a first rheumatoid arthritis trial, and California moved to make households suppliers to the grid. The friction runs alongside the diffusion - Meta's robots reaching into data-center maintenance labor, and some Indiana data centers reportedly staying online while some Gary residents waited nearly two weeks for power. The through-line is capability equalizing into downloadable files and cheaper safety work at the same moment ownership of the rails concentrates.
